description: High-frequency users who keep repurchasing the same daily essentials (milk, bread, eggs, medicines) and rarely leave their narrow set of categories.
goals: Replenish daily staples with one-tap checkout
Avoid any friction in the buying process
Get the same products on time
pain_points: No reason to browse beyond the usual list
shopping_behavior: Repeat same SKUs; use reorder and quick checkout; low dwell time; high frequency but single-category basket.
opportunity: Add a 'Complete your basket' nudge with complementary items before checkout.

description: Users who open the app with a very specific, time-sensitive need and want to complete that single mission as fast as possible.
goals: Get the missing item in minutes
pain_points: No time to browse new categories
shopping_behavior: Search for one item, add to cart, checkout; high delivery-speed sensitivity; will switch apps if ETA is poor.
opportunity: Create 'Forgot Something?' bundles and emergency kits with one-tap add for related categories.

description: Time-poor users who use Blinkit to outsource household shopping. They value saved time and predictable quality over exploring new products.
goals: Trust the platform to deliver good quality
pain_points: No time to discover new categories
shopping_behavior: Prefer scheduled/repeat orders; stick to known categories; rarely browse; will pay for convenience.
opportunity: Build a 'Personal Store' with auto-replenishment and one new curated category per month.

description: Price-sensitive users who actively look for offers, cashback and bundles. They are the most likely to try a new category if the deal is attractive.
goals: Try new things at low risk
pain_points: Discounts are usually on categories they already buy
Discovery for value products in new categories is weak
shopping_behavior: Browse offers, compare prices, add items only when discounted, open to cross-category if deal is strong.
opportunity: Introduce 'Explore & Save' cross-category offers such as 20% off the first purchase in a new category.

description: Users who prioritise freshness, expiry, packaging and brand trust. They stay in known categories because quality in new categories feels unproven.
pain_points: Worry about quality when trying new categories
Limited product information for new SKUs
shopping_behavior: Inspect product details, reviews and expiry; prefer known brands; negative experiences reduce trust in other categories.
opportunity: Add quality badges, expiry visibility, customer photos and freshness guarantees for new-category products.
